bodies.intuition: The learning rate decides how far to move on each step. Too small and training takes forever; too large and it overshoots and diverges. It is the single most important number in a training run, and the range that works spans about one order of magnitude.
bodies.engineer: Almost never held constant in practice. The workable maximum scales with batch size and shrinks as the model gets larger, and the standard way to find it is a short sweep rather than any principled derivation. A run that diverges in the first few hundred steps is almost always this parameter.
bodies.math: θ ← θ − η∇L. Stability requires η below roughly 2/λ_max of the loss Hessian, which is neither known nor stationary. Linear scaling η ∝ |B| holds empirically over a wide batch range, breaking down at the top of it.

emphasis.intuition: the single most important number in a training run
